detailed_rationale:
Shaily Engineering Plastics is a contract manufacturer of precision plastic/metal components serving consumer (home furnishings, FMCG packaging, LED lighting) and healthcare/pharma delivery-device clients, including a toy-manufacturing partnership with Spin Master. FY26 results were strong on the surface: revenue grew 26% YoY (Rs.991 crore vs Rs.787 crore) and net profit grew 83% (Rs.170 crore vs Rs.93 crore), with operating margin expanding from 15% (FY22) to 28% (FY26) -- a genuine multi-year structural improvement from operating leverage and mix shift toward higher-value consumer and healthcare components, not a single-quarter one-off (no asset sale, tax credit or merger effect identified). ROE and ROCE are strong at roughly 27% and 29% respectively.

The growth quality needs a caveat, however: net profit growth (83%) has vastly outpaced revenue growth (26%) for two years running, which is the classic signature of operating leverage off a fixed cost base as the company scales -- a real phenomenon, but one that decelerates once margins approach a ceiling (28% OPM is already high for a contract manufacturer, leaving less room for further margin-driven profit outperformance versus revenue growth). At the same time, the working capital cycle has stretched from 114 to 135 days, meaning growth is consuming more cash than before, which is worth watching, especially since the company is also onboarding two new global retail-chain clients (supply ramp expected through FY26/27) -- a positive for revenue but a client-concentration and execution risk typical of contract manufacturing.

Promoter holding has declined from ~43.7% to ~41.1%, a modest dilution trend, though nothing suggesting distress; the company continues to invest in capacity for new client wins and engages with global investors (UBS analyst meetings), consistent with an ambitious growth phase. Nothing here points to fabricated or one-off-driven numbers -- the FY26 beat looks like genuine operating leverage -- but the current ~73x P/E prices in a continuation of the extraordinary profit growth rate rather than the more moderate, margin-plateauing trajectory that operating leverage math would suggest from here.
recommendation_rationale: Quant composite is Hold (3y 52.6 / 1y 48.8) and the underlying story supports that: genuine, structural margin improvement and strong execution, but growth of this magnitude (83% profit growth) cannot repeat indefinitely once margins near their ceiling, and the ~73x multiple already prices in a lot of continued outperformance. No rescue or escalation warranted -- ordinary valuation-versus-growth tension, not a methodology gap.
summary: Shaily has delivered standout growth -- 26% revenue growth and 83% profit growth in FY26 -- driven by genuine operating leverage as margins expanded from 15% to 28% over four years, alongside new global retail-client wins. But margins are now high enough that further profit growth will likely track revenue growth more closely rather than outpace it as dramatically, and working capital use has increased as the business has scaled. At roughly 73x earnings, the stock is priced for continued exceptional execution, leaving limited room for a slower year.
positive_para: A genuine multi-year margin story: operating margin nearly doubled (15% to 28%) as the business scaled and shifted mix toward higher-value consumer, healthcare and toy-manufacturing components, translating into ROE/ROCE in the high-20s%. New client wins from two global retail chains give visible revenue ramp through FY26/27, and the balance sheet is manageable with declining absolute borrowings.
negative_para: The 83% profit growth rate is a product of margin expansion that is now approaching a natural ceiling for a contract manufacturer (28% OPM), so the extreme profit-outpacing-revenue pattern of the last two years is unlikely to repeat -- future growth should look more like revenue growth (high-teens to 20s%) than the eye-popping profit numbers investors have gotten used to. Working capital days have stretched from 114 to 135, meaning growth is consuming incrementally more cash, and reliance on a handful of large global clients (new retail-chain wins, Spin Master partnership) concentrates execution risk. At ~73x earnings, there is very little valuation cushion if any of these growth levers disappoint.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~73x trailing earnings, the market is pricing in growth well above 20% sustained for several years. The business can plausibly deliver high-teens-to-20% growth on new client ramps, but the specific driver of the last two years' profit outperformance -- margin expansion -- is close to exhausted at 28% OPM, so profit growth should converge toward revenue growth from here. ROE (~27%) is strong and the growth has not required heavy dilution, but the current multiple leaves little room for the deceleration that operating-leverage math implies is coming.
